findings.problem: TODO claims Rayon and SmallVec will be faster for a fixed [u8; 4] input without any benchmark, workload, or measurement evidence
findings.failure_mode: Rayon task-scheduling overhead, thread-pool setup cost, and SmallVec heap allocation fallback will all exceed the work of classifying four bytes, producing a measurable regression rather than improvement
findings.fix: Remove the Rayon/SmallVec TODO; return [&'static str; 4] directly to eliminate all allocation and parallel overhead for this fixed-size input

findings.problem: Function returns Vec<&'static str> for a fixed [u8; 4] input, forcing a heap allocation on every call
findings.failure_mode: Every invocation allocates a Vec header plus four &str pointers on the heap, causing allocator pressure, cache misses, and unpredictable tail latency for a computation that produces exactly four known-size elements
findings.fix: Change signature to fn classify_four(bytes: &[u8; 4]) -> [&'static str; 4] and build the result as a fixed array, eliminating all heap allocation

findings.problem: The TODO makes a performance claim ("it will be faster") without workload description, target hardware, baseline measurement, regression threshold, or any benchmark command evidence
findings.failure_mode: Unmeasured optimization introduces complexity (Rayon thread pool, SmallVec dependency) that may degrade latency, increase binary size, and violate the Holzman rule that faster code wins only when measured
findings.fix: Delete the claim; if parallelism is genuinely needed for a different workload, add a benchmark with workload/hardware/baseline/new-number evidence before introducing Rayon

findings.problem: Iterator .collect() into Vec creates an intermediate heap-allocated collection for four elements that could be stored in a stack array
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per call; .collect() must guess capacity or grow, adding branching and memory traffic for a fixed four-element output
findings.fix: Replace iterator+collect with a fixed array ["even"; 4] built via a bounded loop or explicit array construction, returning the array by value

findings.problem: A TODO comment in production source encodes an incorrect optimization strategy (Rayon + SmallVec for 4-byte input) that will mislead future edits
findings.failure_mode: Future developers may implement the suggested change, regressing performance and adding an external dependency (rayon crate) for no benefit
findings.fix: Remove the TODO and replace the body with a correct fixed-array implementation

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for classify_four or any performance claim about Rayon/SmallVec
no profiler data showing classify_four as a hot path bottleneck
no allocation profile (e.g., flamegraph or heaptrack) comparing Vec vs fixed-array return
no second-ring evidence (assembly, cache-miss counters, or p50/p95/p99 latency measurements) supporting the performance claim
residual_risk: Static review only; no cargo commands executed. The code compiles and has no panic surfaces, unchecked arithmetic, or unsafe. The primary risk is that the TODO comment drives future developers to implement Rayon/SmallVec, which will measurably regress performance on this fixed-4-element workload. Removing the TODO and returning a fixed array eliminates all identified issues.
